clue.text: Fight about nothing, having run into girl

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for nothing is read backwards

parts.note: FA is short for 'sweet Fanny Adams', British slang for nothing at all

indicators.note: into says the run goes inside the girl's name

parts.note: Fay is a girl's name
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Someone started a brawl over nothing after barging into a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns FA round to AF. FA is 'sweet Fanny Adams', British slang for nothing, a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: An affray is a public brawl, a disturbance of the peace by fighting.

clue.text: 22 film part, introducing a short story a couple of times

indicators.note: introducing means the following letters are brought inside the word for part

parts.note: a fraction is a part of a whole

indicators.note: short tells us to cut the last letter off the word for story

parts.note: a tale is a story

indicators.note: a couple of means the abbreviation is taken twice

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, as in maths 'times'

explanation.surface: A piece about a film starring the 22 actor, with a brief story told twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introducing' puts ATALATT inside after the first letter of the part word. '22 film' means a film starring the actor at 22 across.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1987 thriller starred the actor clued at 22 across opposite Glenn Close.

clue.text: Polanski "film" about great 24 22 film

parts.note: Roman Polanski is the film director, so his first name is used

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the film word goes round the next pieces

parts.note: cine is a short word for film or cinema
GT is the abbreviation for great, as in Gt Britain
24 refers to the clue at 24 down, a performer; Charlton Heston was a great one

explanation.surface: Polanski is making a 'film' about a great performer, apparently a 22 film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the film word round GT and the actor, giving CINGTHESTONE. The quotation marks around "film" hint that the word is used for its letters, not as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1984 adventure comedy starred the actor clued at 22 across with Kathleen Turner.

clue.text: Showed tiredness on break of new day

indicators.note: a break of the words breaks them up so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone yawned as the new day dawned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break of' looks like 'break of day', dawn, but it scrambles NEW DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening the mouth wide involuntarily is what a sleepy or bored person does.

clue.text: Quiet position on river estuary primarily used for bivouac

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
to sit is to be placed or positioned

indicators.note: primarily means the word estuary gives only its first letter

explanation.surface: A quiet spot by a river mouth is chosen for a night's camp outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A bivouac is a temporary camp, and a camping ground is where one is made.

clue.text: Scottish fellow gets out-of-this-world peace pipe

parts.note: Calum is a typically Scottish man's name
ET is the extra-terrestrial, from the film

explanation.surface: A Scotsman acquires a wonderful pipe of peace.
explanation.definitionFit: A calumet is the ceremonial tobacco pipe of North American peoples, smoked to seal peace.

clue.text: 5D's new wine

indicators.note: new says the letters are made fresh in another order

parts.note: 5 down's answer, with the possessive taken as an S, gives the fodder letters

explanation.surface: The peace pipe has a new drink to go with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the letters of the 5 down answer plus S into the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscatel is a sweet wine made from muscat grapes.

clue.text: Society backing open country

indicators.note: backing means the word for open is read backwards

parts.note: airy means open and spacious

explanation.surface: A club supports open land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the word for open into YRIA; in a down clue it reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a nation of the Middle East.

clue.text: To that man breaking out -rent to be reviewed

indicators.note: breaking means the man splits the other letters by getting inside them
to be reviewed suggests the letters are looked at again in a new order

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man breaks into a dispute over rent that needs reviewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be reviewed' rearranges OUT RENT to TREUNTO, and 'breaking' puts HE inside after T.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereunto is an old formal word meaning to that thing or place.

clue.text: One's out of place by top of mine shaft

indicators.note: out of means the numeral one is taken away from the word for place

parts.note: a site is a place
I is the Roman numeral one; One's reads as One is

indicators.note: top of means only the first letter of mine is used

explanation.surface: Something is missing beside the head of a mine shaft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes I from SITE leaving STE; 'top of' gives M.
explanation.definitionFit: A stem is a slender shaft, as of a plant or a pipe.

clue.text: Bank loses over cutting source of funds for 22 film

indicators.note: cutting means the shortened bank is put inside the purse

parts.note: a wallet is where one's cash is drawn from

indicators.note: loses means a letter is dropped from the word for bank

parts.note: a store is a bank, as in a store of supplies
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A bank is losing money it was meant to supply for a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' drops O to leave STRE, which 'cutting' puts inside the purse word. 'Bank' suggests money, but here it is a stockpile.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1987 Oliver Stone drama won the actor at 22 across an Oscar as Gordon Gekko.

clue.text: Churchill's home help, a nimble dancing master

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and land in a new order

parts.note: an ace is an expert or master

explanation.surface: Winston Churchill's domestic help is an agile dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges the letters into BLENHEIMPAL. Churchill was born at this Oxfordshire stately home.
explanation.definitionFit: Blenheim Palace in Oxfordshire was Churchill's birthplace and ancestral family seat.

clue.text: Builders()

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Builders()' is cut short: the blog says a double definition (Bob the Builder and a shilling) but the second definition's words are missing and not found.

clue.text: 22 film artist faithfully reproduced in spell interrupted by cold

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is taken as an artist
sic is printed to show a quotation is copied exactly as found

indicators.note: interrupted by means the word for spell has cold placed inside it

parts.note: a stint is a spell of work
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: An artist's work faithfully copied appears in a period broken up by a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupted by' puts C inside STINT to make STINCT.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1992 erotic thriller starred the actor at 22 across with Sharon Stone.

clue.text: Zombie relative mostly eats "killer" fruit

indicators.note: eats means the shortened relative takes the fruit inside it
mostly means the last letter of the relative is dropped

parts.note: an aunt is a relative
a tomato is botanically a fruit, and 'killer' recalls the film about killer tomatoes

explanation.surface: A zombie relative is devouring a man-eating tomato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' leaves AUN and 'eats' puts the fruit inside. "Killer" alludes to the cult film Attack of the Killer Tomatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: An automaton is a mindless robot-like being, just as a zombie acts without will.

clue.text: See 3
Newspaper on strike gets through the disruption

indicators.note: gets through means the following pieces pass into the scrambled word
disruption says the word the is thrown into a new order

parts.note: on and leg both name the same side of a cricket field
to rap is to strike sharply

explanation.surface: A newspaper on strike still manages to get through the disruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disruption' gives TEH and 'gets through' puts the cricket and strike words inside it. In cricket the on side is also called the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Telegraph is a British broadsheet newspaper.

clue.text: Congestion on major road could do for islander

parts.note: a jam is traffic congestion
the A1 is Britain's main road north from London, written AI
can means to be able, like could

explanation.surface: A traffic jam on a major road might finish off someone from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the longest numbered road in Britain, and crosswords write the 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jamaican is a native of the Caribbean island of Jamaica.

clue.text: Test driver felt answer would get very good marks?

parts.note: The Stig is the anonymous test driver on the BBC motoring show Top Gear
to mat is to felt or tangle fibres together

explanation.surface: A test driver feels the answer deserves top grades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very good' means saintly here: these are marks of holiness, not exam scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Stigmata are wounds like Christ's appearing on saints, so holy marks.

clue.text: Salt's energy shown in menu, only for the fit?

parts.note: a salt is a sailor, and AB is an able seaman

indicators.note: shown in means the energy letter is placed inside the menu word

parts.note: a menu is a list of dishes
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A sailor's energetic dish appears on a menu suited only to healthy people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown in' places E inside the menu word. Salt is old slang for an experienced sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An ableist attitude discriminates against disabled people, favouring the fit and healthy.

clue.text: Old link fences, steel perhaps

indicators.note: fences means the word for link encloses the old letter

parts.note: to ally is to link or join

explanation.surface: An old chain-link fence is made of steel, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel is a mixture of iron and carbon, an example of a metal blend.

clue.text: Those finishing surgery bandage us very well

indicators.note: those finishing means the letters that end each of the next words

explanation.surface: Surgeons finishing an operation bandage patients up very well.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the final letter of surgery, bandage and us.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Very well' is an expression of agreement or consent.

clue.text: Spring, as black cat

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an ounce is the snow leopard, a big cat

explanation.surface: A black cat leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring is to leap or rebound, as a ball does.

clue.text: 24, so much legal aid is free

indicators.note: free means the letters are released to take a new order

explanation.surface: So much legal aid is given free of charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges SO MUCH LEGAL AID. The definition is the answer to 24 down, a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Douglas is an American film star, so a performer of the kind clued at 24 down.

clue.text: Insertion mark visible in scar etc.

indicators.note: visible in means the letters can be seen inside the words scar etc.

explanation.surface: An insertion mark can be seen in the word 'scar' and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: A caret is the inverted-V proofreading symbol showing where text is to be added.

clue.text: I'm in a part but not female

definitions.text: I'm in a part but not female

indicators.note: but not means the female abbreviation is taken out of the word for a part

parts.note: a factor is a part or element

explanation.surface: Someone says they are playing a role, though not as a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes a male performer; 'but not' drops F from FACTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A male performer plays a part, and the feminine counterpart is an actress.

clue.text: See 2
Some appear typically pretentious

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people often appear pretentious.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty describes a showy, affected interest in the arts.

clue.text: See 12
Late run interrupts popular press

parts.note: ex means former or late, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: interrupts means the run letter breaks into the word for popular

parts.note: hot means popular or in demand
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A late run of stories disrupts the popular press.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhort is to urge or press someone strongly.
